bug_description: Python's own parser could not read this code because an opening parenthesis in a function call is never closed, so the file fails to parse at all.
solution: Add the missing closing parenthesis right after the last argument in the call.

bug_description: Python's own parser could not read this code because the colon at the end of a function definition or if statement is missing, so the file fails to parse at all.
solution: Add the missing colon at the end of the def/if/for/while line.

bug_description: This closing curly brace has no matching opening bracket anywhere before it in the file - an extra brace was left after the function's real closing brace, which will fail the build with an unexpected token error.
solution: Delete the extra closing brace, or add the missing opening brace it was meant to close earlier in the file.

error: This '{' was opened here but was never closed
bug_description: A curly brace opened for a method or class body is never closed anywhere in the rest of the file, so the compiler cannot determine where that block ends.
solution: Add the missing closing brace at the point where this method or block is meant to end.

fixed_code:
const items = getItems();
const total = items.reduce((sum, x) => sum + x, 0);
bug_description: A closing bracket does not match the type of bracket that was opened earlier - a parenthesis was used where a curly brace was expected to close a block, so the parser cannot line up the brackets correctly.
solution: Replace the mismatched bracket with the correct closing character, or check whether an earlier bracket in this block was closed at the wrong spot.

bug_description: A quoted string starts on this line but the line ends before a matching closing quote is found, usually caused by a missing closing quote character.
solution: Add the missing closing quote at the end of the string so it matches the quote character that opened it.

error: Unterminated template literal at end of file
bug_description: A template literal using backticks is opened but never closed before the end of the file, so every backtick that opens one needs exactly one matching backtick to close it.
solution: Add the missing closing backtick to complete the template string.

fixed_code:

bug_description: A block comment is opened with /* but the closing */ is never found, so everything after it in the file is silently treated as a comment, which can hide real code.
solution: Add the missing closing */ to end the comment block, then check nothing important got silently swallowed by it.

buggy_code:
def calculate_total(price, quantity):
    total = price * quantity
    return total
    print("This line will never run")
bug_description: This code sits right after a return statement in the same block, so it can never actually execute no matter what path the program takes.
solution: Delete the unreachable code - removing it has no effect on behavior since it never ran in the first place.

bug_description: Every branch of this if/else statement returns a value, so any code placed after the whole if/else block can never be reached no matter which branch runs.
solution: Delete the code after the if/else block, since every possible path through it already exits the function.

bug_description: There is a closing curly brace here with no matching opening bracket anywhere before it in the file, which is the exact class of error a JavaScript bundler reports as an unexpected token and will fail the build.
solution: Remove the extra closing brace, checking nearby lines to confirm which one doesn't belong.
